findings.reason: without the edge the plan's own readiness surface advertises a node whose one file is claimed by a live run, and the collision it names is exactly what the DAG exists to prevent.
findings.text: §59 says `reckon/serve.py` "is claimed by the-cached-index-absorbs-each-change (run `r-20261024T030624268974`), so this section dispatches after that run lands", yet `plan-section-depends-on` has no `s59` key at all, and the constraint lives only in prose the roadmap's DAG never reads, so a dispatcher sees §59 as ready and can launch it against a tree where that run holds the same file

findings.reason: a citation to a non-existent plan is unresolvable, and here the citation carries the only record of which work must land first.
findings.text: §59 names the plan `the-cached-index-absorbs-each-change` as the holder of `reckon/serve.py`, but `grep -rln` for that slug across `docs/` returns only this plan file and `find docs/plans -name '*cached*index*'` returns nothing, so the holder cannot be looked up by any later reader, and a section dependency could not be written against it either

findings.reason: the case cannot separate head from base unless it first warms the cache, so a worker following it literally writes a test that is red at base and head alike and reports nothing about the fix.
findings.text: §59's first case requires that "one call walks each tree's discovery signature exactly once: the project's tree … and the mounted project's tree, reached from `_external_project_signatures`", but on a cold `_DISC_CACHE` `discover_plans` (`reckon/serve.py:1535`) skips its first branch and `_fresh_discovery` (`reckon/serve.py:1501-1515`) returns before calling `_external_project_signatures`, so the mounted tree is walked zero times and the "exactly once" arm fails on the unfixed tree for the wrong reason

findings.reason: the current deliverable changes nothing about which claims are judged, so no node's mechanism rests on the sentence, and correcting it would tidy the Why rather than redirect work.
findings.text: §58's Why says the claims matter because "Both compare a claim's paths with the write paths of open sections", but `_held_paths_by_section` (`reckon/roadmap.py:2634`) groups over every key in `section_runs` and never consults open sections, and only `_overlapping_scope_findings` (`reckon/roadmap.py:1584`) filters through `open_by_plan` — and this sentence is a remainder of the replaced filter deliverable, not of the reuse deliverable now stated

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §59 cites the plan `the-cached-index-absorbs-each-change`, which resolves to no file under `docs/plans/`; every other anchor in the three units resolves against the tree.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §59's first case asserts the mounted project's tree is walked "exactly once", a count reachable only when `_DISC_CACHE` is already warm.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — each unit writes its gate log and evidence fragment under `docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline/`, and each gate log is required to name its revision and end in `EXIT=`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags reach the symbols or filenames the three units add.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §58's Why still argues from open-section path filtering, which the replaced deliverable no longer performs.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §56 (store every composition, answer stale inside the deadline), §58 (reuse one stopped claim's git answer) and §59 (one signature walk per discovery region) each name one deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §59 states it "dispatches after" the run that holds `reckon/serve.py`, but carries no `plan-section-depends-on` entry, so nothing in the section DAG delays it.
